name: Othniel (Caleb's nephew, Achsah's husband)
title: Israel's first judge
summary: Othniel was the first judge in Israel after Joshua's death. He was the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, and won Achsah's hand by capturing the city of Kiriath-sepher. God raised him up to deliver Israel from Cushan-rishathaim's oppression, and the land had peace for forty years under his leadership.

keyEvents.title: The Capture of Kiriath-sepher
keyEvents.description: Othniel captured the city of Kiriath-sepher (also called Debir) and thereby won Achsah, Caleb's daughter, as his wife as a reward for his bravery.

keyEvents.title: Achsah's Dowry
keyEvents.description: When Achsah came to Othniel, she persuaded her father Caleb to give her springs of water in addition to the land of the Negev as her dowry.

keyEvents.title: Called to Be Judge
keyEvents.description: When Israel had sinned and been oppressed by Cushan-rishathaim from Mesopotamia for eight years, they cried out to the Lord, and he raised up Othniel as their deliverer.

keyEvents.title: The Spirit of the Lord upon Othniel
keyEvents.description: The Spirit of the Lord came upon Othniel, and he became judge in Israel. He went out to war, and the Lord gave Cushan-Rishathaim into his hand.

keyEvents.title: Forty Years of Peace
keyEvents.description: After Othniel's victory, the land had peace for forty years, until Othniel died. This marked the first period of rest during the time of the judges.
